Direct h5 comparison (check_61_1.py): target == inv(A) bit-exactly (max|diff| 0.0, 0.0, 1.8e-20 on tests 0-2) where A = direct-lattice column matrix with a//x, b in xy plane; Busing-Levy misses by 7.4e-6 (tests 0,1, > rtol*|tgt|=1.9e-6) and 0.044 (test 2, gamma=120.1). Decisive attack on any defensible-convention escape: tgt.T@tgt - G* = 2.7e-6 / 0.027 (tests 0/2) while tgt@tgt.T - G* = 0, so the target violates |B@hkl|^2 = hkl^T G* hkl and is NOT a valid hkl->q transform in ANY Cartesian frame -- it is the transpose of one (rows, not columns, are the reciprocal primitive vectors, and they live in the direct-lattice-aligned frame x//a, not the stated x*//a*: target column 0 = (0.18549537,0,0) but a* = 0.18550273). Every prompt-compliant solution fails; only the row-stacked/transposed object passes.
